To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solvent relaxation kinetics of mixed cation/zwitterionic lipid membrane depends non-monotonically on the content of cationic component and that the hydration increases with the cationic lipid amount.

the mixed lipid membrane consisting of cetyltrimethylammoniopropane and phosphatidylcholines exhibits nonmonotonic behavior of the solvent relaxation kinetics and that the slowest solvent dynamics are observed for 45 mol % of the cationic lipid.
the solvent relaxation kinetics in mixed cationic bilayers is nonmonotonic and depends on the lipid composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of cationic membrane components on membrane properties, and the results can be used to improve the design of cationic liposomes as nonviral vectors.
the properties of the mixed cationic membranes and the influence of the lipid chain length on the membrane properties.
the properties of mixed DMTAP/DMPC bilayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cationic lipid bilayers are more hydrated than zwitterionic ones, which is in line with the literature.
the solvent relaxation kinetics is sensitive to the membrane structure and its hydration, which are in turn influenced by the presence of cationic lipids in the membrane.
the solvent relaxation measurements of Laurdan in mixed cationic lipid bilayers can be used to monitor the membrane structure and its changes upon the cationic lipid addition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cationic lipid in the membrane is not only responsible for the electrostatic charge of the surface, but also affects the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance of the membrane.
the cationic lipid molecules in the mixed cationic bilayer are not homogeneously distributed.
the cationic lipids in the membrane are able to increase its hydration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cationic lipid concentration at which the membrane reaches the highest hydration depends on its acyl chain length.
Laurdan is an effective probe for the study of cationic membranes.
the solvent relaxation measurements can be used to characterize mixed cationic membranes.
